A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MissTSM work. The main text, figures, equations, tables, and Appendices A–I are readable and support matching content across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original MissTSM forecasting and classification results, component ablations, computational measurements, and an anomaly-handling case study.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds computational profiling, scalability experiments, SAITS tuning experiments, and LSTM backbone evaluations.

M1.justification: The TFI embedding, positional encoding, shared-query masked cross-attention, and backbone integration procedure remain unchanged. LSTM experiments apply the existing wrapper. The newly disclosed default MAE implementation without input-shape projection does not establish an underlying method change.

E1.justification: Appendix D.3 adds synthetic scalability data covering increasingly high-dimensional inputs, with tabulated measurements for 10–800 variates. Existing application coverage remains: P12, P19, Solar-Energy, and the PSM case study were already included in v2's appendices.

E2.justification: v3 adds LSTM+SAITS and LSTM+Spline comparisons against LSTM+MissTSM in Tables 20–21, and SAITS+MAE in the P19 computational comparison. Existing forecasting and clinical comparator sets are retained; promoting the P12/P19 comparison into the main text adds no comparators.

E3.justification: New protocols include P19 runtime, throughput, and peak-memory profiling with batch size 64 and mixed precision disabled; dimensionality scaling with fixed context length 336 and embedding dimension 16; and a 27-configuration SAITS search selecting configurations using test results. These extend the evaluation design rather than replace the retained benchmark protocols.

E4.justification: v3 adds analyses of computational scaling with feature count, sensitivity of comparisons to SAITS tuning, and portability to a non-transformer LSTM backbone. These test important efficiency and generality questions. Earlier TFI, masking, anomaly, and MAE ablations remain; Section 5.3 relocates existing ablations.

E5.justification: Both versions already report means and standard deviations over five masked-data trials and provide uncertainty for timing measurements. New experiments extend these reporting practices without an explicit increase in runs or new confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation methods.

E6.justification: Retained results match, including v2 Table 20 and v3 Table 26. v3 adds substantial profiling, scaling, tuned-baseline, and LSTM results. For example, Table 17 reports tuned iTransformer+SAITS MSE 0.484 versus the retained default 0.773 for ETTh2 periodic masking at horizon 720; these are different configurations, not a same-setting performance revision.

T1.justification: Appendix D.1 newly derives time, activation-memory, and parameter complexity, including O(LNd^2), O(LNd), and O(d^2+Nd) for MissTSM, and compares asymptotic costs with three baselines. Section 3.3 also corrects the attention-mask implication's sign and the multi-head concatenation endpoint from h to h−1.

C1.justification: Both versions claim a model-agnostic, imputation-free wrapper and competitive forecasting/classification performance, especially with high missingness and weak periodicity. The numbered contributions, additional supporting experiments, and replacement of 'novel' with 'simple' do not materially change these core claims.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive explanations of the shared-query design, computational trade-offs, backward-pass scaling, and high-dimensional limitations. It further qualifies when simple imputation may be preferable. Section 5.2.3 narrows the interpretation of the unchanged lake figure from consistently better performance to competitive performance.

D1.justification: v3 adds a code-access link, clarifies the default MAE integration, documents profiling software and controls, and supplies SAITS search ranges and selected configurations. It also explains observed-only lake MSE, already labeled 'Masked MSE' in v2's figure. Most original implementation and training details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works are retained. Section 3.3 expands the distinction between MissTSM's variate-first aggregation and mTAN's temporal-first processing, and explicitly locates novelty in adapting masked cross-attention to IMTS rather than inventing a new attention mechanism.

P1.justification: v3 restructures the introduction around tokenization and enumerated contributions, promotes clinical comparisons and MAE ablations into the main text, reorganizes experimental subsections, and expands Appendix D into a structured complexity discussion. Dedicated design-choice, limitations, and broader-impact sections further change the narrative organization.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to predominantly single-column presentation, with extensive resizing and relocation of displays. Existing clinical and backbone tables move between the main text and appendix. v3 also adds six tables and two scalability figures; retained plots, including the lake comparison, preserve their underlying results.

improvement.justification: Compared with v2's limited computational case study and transformer-only backbone demonstrations, v3 provides useful scalability evidence, LSTM comparisons, and tuned-baseline checks. The code link and more accurate lake interpretation improve reproducibility and claim calibration. These gains are limited by test-set selection in the SAITS tuning study and insufficiently specified masking conditions for the new LSTM tables.
